patterns.description: All three tickets trace back to the same root cause: Acme Cloud Infrastructure's staffing/resourcing problems on the Data Center Cloud Migration program. HND-310 documents a second cutover rehearsal slip due to Acme staffing shortage, HND-700 shows the escalation about that same slippage going unanswered by both Acme's account exec and the internal VP, and HND-311 (Acme's Security Review, due 10/31) has gone silent the same week -- consistent with the same vendor being stretched thin across multiple parallel deliverables.
patterns.why_it_matters: This isn't three isolated vendor issues -- it's one vendor capacity problem threatening three related deliverables (cutover rehearsal, cutover date, security review) at once. Program lead should escalate directly to Acme leadership this week rather than treating each ticket as a separate risk, and get a consolidated resourcing commitment before 11/07.

patterns.description: Dealer Systems Integration (HND-146c) is blocked waiting on BrightPath for the dealer portal release calendar to push CCPA copy live. HND-520, BrightPath's own status update, explains why: BrightPath is heads-down on an unrelated emergency firmware defect escalated by Honda, with all other requests -- including the dealer portal release calendar -- explicitly paused with no ETA.
patterns.why_it_matters: This is a direct root-cause match: BrightPath's emergency is the reason Dealer Systems can't proceed, and the CCPA due date (10/31) is at real risk since there's no ETA on the calendar confirmation. Program lead should escalate to BrightPath now with a specific ask for a target date, rather than waiting on a vendor response that's explicitly deprioritized.

patterns.description: HND-88 (CDP Team) is blocked waiting on Data Privacy & Legal Ops to confirm the final consent taxonomy, with its due date today (10/25). HND-89, from Data Privacy & Legal Ops itself, confirms the taxonomy review was pushed to next week because the team's bandwidth went to CCPA copy work and an unplanned EU DSAR audit request.
patterns.why_it_matters: The blocker named in HND-88 is directly explained and confirmed by HND-89 -- CDP will miss its due date today because Legal Ops deprioritized the taxonomy review. Program lead should flag this as an already-missed dependency (not just 'at risk') and get Legal Ops to commit a hard date this week to unblock CDP.

patterns.description: Data Privacy & Legal Ops is being pulled in three directions simultaneously: finalizing/distributing CCPA copy (HND-146/HND-201, completed) and now an unplanned EU DSAR audit request, both of which are cited as the reason the consent taxonomy review (HND-89) slipped.
patterns.why_it_matters: Even though each individual CCPA task shows as on_track or complete, the combination confirms Legal Ops has no slack -- the taxonomy review (feeding HND-88's blocked status) is being repeatedly bumped by other legal asks. Program lead should assess whether Legal Ops needs temporary support or reprioritization before more downstream teams stall.

patterns.description: Enterprise Identity & Access Management's SSO cert renewal (HND-610, due 10/26) had two engineers pulled off to triage an unplanned partner integration incident (HND-611), leaving zero schedule buffer. Meanwhile, Mobile App Engineering's Q4 Security Patch (HND-150) is also running tight on 10/25, and Mobile is separately delaying CCPA work (HND-146b) because of that same patch release.
patterns.why_it_matters: Multiple teams are simultaneously running at zero-buffer on overlapping late-October dates due to unplanned incidents diverting resources. Program lead should treat 10/24-10/26 as a high-risk window across IAM and Mobile and check contingency staffing rather than assuming each team's 'still on track' self-report holds if another incident hits.

patterns.description: Five unrelated tickets across Mobile Engineering, Legal Ops, IAM, a vendor (BrightPath), and Marketing all report the same signal: competing_objectives, where unplanned/emergency work (security patch, DSAR audit, partner incident, firmware defect, CMO campaign ask) is displacing previously planned deliverables in the same week.
patterns.why_it_matters: This is a program-wide pattern, not isolated noise -- planned work across nearly every function is being bumped by emergencies in the same week. Program lead should raise this at the leadership level as a capacity/prioritization issue rather than addressing each instance individually, since the volume suggests insufficient slack across the program to absorb unplanned work.
